key_insight: Aggregating pixel-wise segmentation uncertainty with spatially-aware strategies (instead of simple averaging) produces more informative image-level uncertainty scores that significantly improve downstream tasks such as out-of-distribution and failure detection.
problem_solved: Pixel-wise uncertainty maps must be condensed to image-level scores for decisions, but naive aggregation (e.g., mean) discards spatial structure and underperforms at detecting localized errors or OOD cases.
method: Introduce spatially-aware aggregation schemes that weight or pool pixel uncertainties according to segmentation topology (e.g., region size, distance-to-boundary, connected components).
Compute region- and boundary-aware summary statistics (rather than global mean) to form image-level uncertainty estimates.
Empirically evaluate these aggregations across segmentation benchmarks and downstream tasks (OoD / failure detection), showing consistent performance gains on ROC/AUPR metrics.
impact: Provides a simple, model-agnostic way to turn dense uncertainty maps into much more effective image-level signals, improving reliability and safety for practitioners deploying segmentation models in critical applications.
visual_elements: Side-by-side panel: raw image + segmentation + pixel-wise uncertainty heatmap vs. aggregated scores (mean) vs. spatially-aware aggregated score — visually showing better localization and decision separation.
Schematic pipeline: segmentation → pixel uncertainty → spatial-aware aggregator → image-level score → downstream detector (OoD/failure).
Bar/line charts: performance comparison (AUROC / AUPR) of mean vs. several spatial aggregators across datasets/tasks.
Illustration of aggregation concepts: icons for connected components, boundary distance maps, and weighted pooling to convey the methods intuitively.
paper_title: Better than Average: Spatially-Aware Aggregation of Segmentation Uncertainty Improves Downstream Performance
paper_authors: Vanessa Emanuela Guarino, Claudia Winklmayr, Jannik Franzen, Josef Lorenz Rumberger, Manuel Pfeuffer
